Situation1: They briefly mention their day during a casual conversation at home.
Expectation2: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation2: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Story:
It was almost midnight when my phone buzzed, jolting me from a half-sleep. My wife and I had just finished a quiet evening together, sharing snippets of our day over tea. She’d seemed a little distant, and I knew she wanted me to open up more, to really talk about what was on my mind. I promised myself I’d try harder, that I’d be the husband she needed—someone who didn’t just skim the surface.

But now, my best friend’s name flashed on the screen. His voice, when I answered, was raw and broken. He’d just lost a family member, and he needed me—needed someone to listen, to be there, to help him hold it together. I could hear my wife shifting in bed, probably hoping I’d come back soon, maybe even finally talk to her about what was weighing on me. My heart twisted as I realized I couldn’t be both things at once. I wanted to be the open, attentive husband she deserved, but I also couldn’t turn away from a friend in pain. The weight of both expectations pressed down on me, and I sat there, phone in hand, torn between two worlds.
